title: More Than Two Paths
content:
What problem does this solve?
if/else chooses between two paths. Some rules need three or more mutually exclusive outcomes. elif means: if the earlier condition was false, test this next condition.

Start with the behavior
  if points >= 10:
      print("gold")
  elif points >= 5:
      print("silver")
  else:
      print("bronze")
Python checks from top to bottom and stops after the first true branch in this chain.

Order matters
If a broad condition such as >= 5 comes before a stricter >= 10 condition, a value like 14 will match the broad branch first and never reach the stricter one. Put narrower or higher thresholds before broader ones when they overlap.

Vocabulary after the behavior
elif is an additional conditional branch. An if/elif/else chain is mutually exclusive: exactly one branch runs.
concepts: elif adds another test between if and else
Python checks the chain from top to bottom
Only the first true branch runs
Overlapping thresholds must be ordered carefully

examples.title: Three outcomes
examples.explanation: 6 fails the first condition, passes the second, and stops there.

examples.title: Boundary order
examples.explanation: The stricter threshold is checked first so 14 reaches Cleared.

common_mistakes: Using several separate if statements when only one result should be chosen
Putting a broad threshold before a stricter overlapping threshold
Forgetting that Python stops after the first true branch

exercises.title: First matching branch
hints: 12 >= 10 is True, so Python enters the first branch and skips the rest.

exercises.title: Add the middle path
exercises.prompt: Replace the placeholder keyword so a score of 6 prints medium.
exercises.starter_code:
score = 6
if score >= 10:
    print("high")
if score >= 5:  # replace this keyword
    print("medium")
else:
    print("low")
hints: The middle condition should belong to the same decision chain as the first if.
Use the keyword that means 'otherwise, test this next.'
Change the second if to elif.

tests.message: Use elif for the middle path.

exercises.title: Check the boundary
exercises.prompt: What prints when score is exactly 5?
hints: The second condition uses >=, so it includes 5 itself.

exercises.title: Put thresholds in order
exercises.prompt: A value of 14 should be Cleared, but this prints Review. Repair only the decision order; keep the threshold values and status text unchanged.
hints: Both comparisons are individually reasonable; focus on which one Python sees first.
14 also satisfies >= 5, so the broad condition catches it too early.
Move the >= 12 branch before the >= 5 branch.

exercises.title: Readiness status
exercises.prompt: Write readiness_status(supplies). Return "Cleared" for 10 or more, "Review" for 5 through 9, and "Denied" below 5. Use one if/elif/else chain.
hints: Start with the highest threshold so smaller rules cannot catch large values first.
After supplies >= 10 fails, supplies >= 5 identifies the middle band; everything else is Denied.
Use if supplies >= 10, elif supplies >= 5, else, returning one status from each branch.
exercises.success_message: Your function handles both threshold boundaries and values on either side.

exercises.title: Threat labels
exercises.prompt: Write threat_label(level). Return "Severe" for 8 or more, "Elevated" for 4 through 7, and "Low" below 4.
hints: Again, begin with the higher threshold.
The middle branch only needs >= 4 because reaching it already means the >= 8 test failed.
Use if level >= 8, elif level >= 4, else.
exercises.success_message: You transferred the same ordered-threshold idea to a different rule set.
